name: Cacheon
readme:
# Cacheon

Cacheon is an inference-throughput competition built around SGLang and designed
to operate as a Bittensor subnet. Miners submit inspectable GPU-kernel
contributions at registered boundaries in a validator-owned model. Validators
admit those contributions through a typed, isolated pipeline and reward only
improvements that reproduce under the registered throughput and quality policy.

This repository—published as [`latent-to/cacheon`](https://github.com/latent-to/cacheon)—contains
the miner SDK and examples, validator and chain control plane, evaluation
runtime, settlement and incentive machinery, and chain-independent engine
release tooling.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Cacheon is pre-release software. Implemented paths, retained empirical evidence,
> and production readiness are separate claims. Start with the
> [validator first hour](docs/validator-guide/first-hour.md) for what a deployment must prove.

## Start here

| Goal | Documentation |
|---|---|
| Understand the system | [Concepts](docs/get-started/concepts.md) and [architecture overview](docs/architecture/overview.md) |
| Understand why miners participate and how rewards work | [How miners earn rewards](docs/miner-guide/incentives.md) |
| Build a miner contribution | [Miner guide](docs/miner-guide/overview.md) |
| Operate a validator | [Validator guide](docs/validator-guide/overview.md) |
| See what a crown does and does not authorize | [After a crown](docs/engine/integration.md) |
| Review trust boundaries | [Security model](docs/security/threat-model.md) |
| Contribute to the repository | [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) |

The canonical documentation source lives under [`docs/`](docs/) in this
repository and is rendered at [cacheon.ai/docs](https://cacheon.ai/docs/).

## Local correctness loop

Python 3.11 or newer is required.

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -e ".[cpu,dev,release]"

python -m cacheon.cli slots
python -m cacheon.cli scan examples/miner_silu_torch
python -m cacheon.cli verify examples/miner_silu_torch \
  --device cpu \
  --dtype float32
```

`scan` and `verify` are development checks. They do not establish serving
throughput, end-to-end quality, settlement eligibility, or a production
release. Those decisions belong to the validator-owned qualification path
described in the documentation.

## Design boundaries

- The validator owns the model, workload, references, timing, outputs, and
  reward policy. A miner contribution owns only its registered target.
- Candidate build and execution run in validator-owned, no-egress OCI workers;
  wallet and chain-signing authority remain outside candidate lifetimes.
- A single passing qualification is not a crown. Settlement requires an
  independently reproduced pair bound to the same contribution and evaluation
  context.
- Evaluation acceptance and serving are different decisions. Nothing in the
  repository turns a crown into a release; that is a maintainer decision made
  outside it.

See the [product model](docs/architecture/product-model.md) and
[slot contract](docs/architecture/slot-contract.md) for the normative
invariants.

## Tests

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests
```

Documentation checks are described in
[Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md#documentation).

## License

The repository is licensed under [Apache-2.0](LICENSE). Miner submissions are
governed separately by the
[draft submission terms](docs/legal/submission-terms.md); those terms require
legal review before production use.

codeFiles.pyproject.toml:
[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=68"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "cacheon-harness"
version = "0.0.1"
description = "Validator harness for an inference-throughput competition on SGLang"
license = {text = "Apache-2.0"}
requires-python = ">=3.10"
# torch is required but intentionally NOT pinned here: install the build that
# matches the validator's CUDA/SGLang environment first, then `pip install -e .`.
dependencies = [
  # Python 3.11+ has tomllib in the stdlib; 3.10 needs the same parser API.
  "tomli>=2; python_version<'3.11'",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
# CPU dry-run / laptop development: pulls in the torch the core deliberately
# leaves unpinned (a GPU box gets its torch from the sglang/CUDA install
# instead — see docs/dev/gpu-setup.md). `pip install -e ".[cpu,dev]"` is the
# documented no-GPU quickstart. Note: on Linux the default torch wheel bundles
# CUDA libs (heavier download); for a lean CPU-only install do
# `pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu` first.
cpu = ["torch"]
dev = ["pytest>=7", "ruff==0.12.7", "httpx>=0.24"]
dashboard = ["fastapi>=0.100", "uvicorn>=0.23"]
# S3-compatible object stores (Hippius / AWS / MinIO). boto3 is Apache-2.0.
object-store = ["boto3>=1.34"]

[project.scripts]
cacheon = "cacheon.cli:main"

[tool.setuptools]
license-files = ["LICENSE", "NOTICE"]

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
"cacheon" = ["vendor_provenance.json"]
"cacheon.eval" = ["seccomp_moby_v0_2_1.json"]
"cacheon_kernels.collective" = ["*.cu"]

# Installs the Cacheon seam inside every SGLang process (incl. the spawned
# scheduler that runs the model). This is validator-owned code. Select it with
# SGLANG_PLUGINS=cacheon (the eval harness sets this automatically).
[project.entry-points."sglang.srt.plugins"]
cacheon = "cacheon.integrations.sglang_plugin:register"

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
include = ["cacheon*"]
exclude = ["sglang*", "examples*", "tests*"]

[tool.ruff]
# Miner bundles are scanner inputs, not a harness style surface.
extend-exclude = ["examples"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Correctness-only floor (pyflakes + runtime syntax): violations of these
# rules are always defects. Formatting and import-sorting are deliberately
# not enforced yet.
select = ["F", "E9"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Files whose remaining findings are deferred cleanup (snapshot 2026-08-09,
# taken while these paths were under live modification on the launch lane).
# The b300 input/stage aggregators additionally re-export their imports for
# digest-bound private consumers and need explicit `__all__` declarations,
# not import deletion. Shrinking this list is cleanup; growing it is a
# reviewed decision.
"cacheon/chain/evaluation_lease_store.py" = ["F401"]
"cacheon/chain/intake.py" = ["F401"]
"cacheon/chain/remote_evaluation_dispatcher.py" = ["F401"]
"cacheon/chain/remote_worker_spool.py" = ["F401"]
"cacheon/cli.py" = ["F401"]
"cacheon/eval/b300_registered_qualification.py" = ["F401"]
"cacheon/eval/b300_registered_qualification_inputs.py" = ["F401"]
"cacheon/eval/b300_screen_deployment.py" = ["F401"]
"cacheon/eval/b300_screen_stages.py" = ["F401"]
"cacheon/eval/qualification_runner.py" = ["F401", "F402"]
"cacheon/manifest.py" = ["F402"]
"tests/test_b300_registered_qualification.py" = ["F401"]
"tests/test_b300_remote_qualification_adapter.py" = ["F401"]
"tests/test_evaluation_coordinator.py" = ["F401"]
"tests/test_evaluation_lease_operator.py" = ["F841"]
"tests/test_remote_evaluation_dispatcher.py" = ["F401"]
